summary: Iteration 4 (final regression). Backend: 29/29 pytest PASS when run serially. Frontend: verified admin login, Genera Turni, Stampa/PDF (window.print invoked), Substitution modal (7 candidates + mark-absence-btn), Skill Matrix (40 mezzo + 112 giro toggles), Assenze CRUD page, Driver login with read-only /tabellone (I miei turni + full board, zero admin controls), and driver RBAC blocked from /formazioni (redirects to /tabellone). All requirements A-E validated.

minor.issue: TestAbsences, TestGenerateSpecificWeek and TestRecovery all target the same week (2026-06-01). When xdist splits them across workers, concurrent /shifts/generate calls can race and make TestRecovery::test_recover_creates_makeup flaky (StopIteration when re-fetching original shift). Serial run passes 29/29. Not a product bug — a test-isolation issue.

action_items: Optional: give each pytest class its own week_start (e.g. 2026-06-08, 2026-06-15) to remove the xdist race on /shifts/generate. Product code is unaffected.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py recover_shift correctly re-inserts a new shift and marks the original 'recovered'. OK.
SkillMatrix uses Radix Checkbox — toggle state is on data-state attribute (not class). Persistence covered by TestDriverCRUD.test_crud_and_skills.
Driver correctly redirected from /formazioni to /tabellone; no admin data-testid buttons rendered for driver role.
Substitution modal shows recover-btn only when the shift is uncovered; mark-absence-btn shows when assigned. Behavior matches spec.

success_rate.backend: 100% (29/29 serial); ~97% (28/29) with xdist due to shared week

seed_data_creation: None new; used existing seeded data. Test data created inside tests is cleaned up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full regression complete. Run backend suite with `pytest backend/tests/backend_test.py -n 0` to avoid xdist week-collision flakiness, or refactor per action_items. Frontend testids of note: generate-shifts-btn, print-board-btn, substitution-modal, shift-{uuid}, skill-v-{driver}-{vehicle}, skill-r-{driver}-{route}, mark-absence-btn, recover-btn, close-modal-btn, add-absence-btn.
rca of the issue: TestRecovery flake RCA: The three classes touching week 2026-06-01 (TestAbsences, TestGenerateSpecificWeek, TestRecovery) run in different xdist workers. /shifts/generate wipes and re-creates the week's shifts, so a shift-id captured by TestRecovery can be gone by the time it re-fetches. Reproduction: pytest -n auto. Mitigation: assign distinct week_start values per class (or use pytest-xdist --dist=loadfile grouping in pytest.ini).
